analysis.title: Wall Street's Week From Hell Panic, Liquidations And The Next Big Trade
key_insights: Thursday produced the largest one-day change in markets since Covid, pushing volatility back toward Liberation Day levels. The GS vol desk called it the most panic in a very long time.
GS Prime reports TMT hedge funds took a hit of more than 400bp in one day. Hedge funds are roughly flat to slightly positive YTD, down from about +24% before the June/July AI sell-off.

Nomura says discretionary traders are front-running systematic deleveraging, leveraged ETF rebalancing and dealer hedging. Dealers hold roughly $7bn of negative gamma per 1% SPX move, which creates a theoretical risk of a self-reinforcing selling spiral.

Knowing dealer gamma exposure does not make the flows easy to trade. Dealers may have already sold in anticipation, adjusted hedges intraday or cut exposure before the close, so the timing and size of the selling are uncertain.

Vol-control funds sold risk heavily over the past week. They trade mechanically on volatility, and Nomura says most models do not account for liquidity risk realistically, which showed up the previous day.
Taiwan broke down. EWT closed below its 200-day moving average for the first time since April 2025 and is more oversold than on only a handful of occasions in the past decade.
The Market Ear flagged EWT downside via puts on October 29. The EWT December 95 put has since risen sharply, and the note says it is time to book gains.
INDA and SOX have moved in an almost perfect inverse relationship during the AI selloff. The Market Ear advises against getting too greedy on the India relative-performance trade at current levels.
JPM says India's rolling 12-month performance versus emerging markets recently hit its weakest level in two decades, lagging by roughly 60 percentage points.
BofA's Hartnett says SOX trades 17% below its 200-day moving average. Since 1996, readings of 20-25% below have historically marked attractive entry points.
BofA's Hartnett cites a survey in which 76% of voters oppose new data centers in their communities. He describes the backlash as a growing problem for the AI buildout.

tension_points.bull_case: SOX is 17% below its 200-day moving average, nearing the 20-25% zone that has historically offered attractive entries since 1996 (BofA).
tension_points.bear_case: Systematic selling from vol-control funds, leveraged ETF rebalancing and dealer negative gamma ($7bn per 1% SPX move) could extend the unwind (Nomura).
tension_points.what_invalidates: A move beyond the 20-25% discount to the 200-day without stabilization would show the washout is a continuation of the unwind rather than an entry point.
